start_state: inputs/pew2020_start_state.csv (Pew 2020; no 2010, so no Pew 2010-2020 test window)

start_state.detail: committed Pew 2020 start state (201 countries); Pew 2010 unavailable

bilateral_stock.detail: undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_destination_and_origin.xlsx: 68941 country pairs x years, years [np.int64(1990), np.int64(1995), np.int64(2000), np.int64(2005), np.int64(2010), np.int64(2015), np.int64(2020), np.int64(2024)] (cached parse)

migrant_religion.detail: no country-level Pew migrant file; religion of migrants from the affinity model calibrated to Pew published aggregates (inputs/migrant_religion_published.csv)

religion_fertility.detail: 8 world, 5 regional (2 regions), 10 country figures (4 countries); 7 rows held back

scenarios.stabilising: Historical trends gradually stabilising (reference): after 2100 switching fades (half-life 150 years) to 30% of its 2100 level
scenarios.high_retention: High religious retention and slower conversion
scenarios.rising_migration: Increasing international migration and religious diversity
scenarios.changing_migration: Changing migration patterns (networks fade; geography and demographic pressure dominate)
scenarios.persistent_fertility_gaps: Changing fertility differences: within-country religious fertility gaps persist
scenarios.combined_dispersal: Combined: secularization continues, migration rises, fertility gaps persist

forecast_error_model.note: predictive intervals (pi*) to 2100 add resampled past forecast errors to every run; see religion_forecast/errors.py

switching_survey_level.note: survey level = fitted rates shifted so adults 18-54 match Pew 2025 (117 countries); runs mix the two levels

cautions: Shares after 2100 rest on stated long-run assumptions; 2500 and 3026 are exploratory scenarios without predictive intervals.
q05/q95 are parameter uncertainty only; use pi05/pi95 (to 2100) for predictive intervals.
The Folk/Traditional vs Other split of Pew data is a WRP-based proxy; WRP and Pew classify China differently.

Fertility gaps come from published world, regional or country figures (fertility_evidence.csv); the world and regional tiers are damped because a ratio measured across countries is not a within-country ratio.
The religion of migrants comes from a two-parameter model (minority effect, destination affinity) calibrated to Pew aggregates; corridor-level religion of migrants is not observed.
